title: Cross-functional Launch Readiness Scorecard and Preflight Automation for Runtime / Console / API
creator: Priya Patel
description: Goal: Create a compact, machine-readable Launch Readiness Scorecard and runbook that automatically executes preflight checks across runtime, console, and API layers. Outcome: a single readiness score (0-100) with pass/fail gates, automated smoke checks, and an actionable dashboard + Slack alerts so PMs/Eng/SREs can sign off on canary and wide rollouts without ad-hoc manual validation. Motivation: recent launches have been slowed by manual checklist confusion, inconsistent telemetry cutoffs, and unclear rollback criteria. This initiative standardizes signals, automates verification, and ties the result into our release automation (Launch Conductor).
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard schema defined and documented (JSON schema) and validated by Eng, SRE, and Design
Automated preflight job executes in CI or Launch Conductor pre-cutover and returns a score within 5 minutes for typical change sets
Dashboard tile in Console shows last-run score, signal breakdown, and timestamp; links to failing checks
Slack channel integration posts pass/fail with direct link to rollback playbook and on-call roster
Canary rollout automation gates on score >= 80 (configurable); manual override requires 2 approvers and written justification
Playbook includes deterministic rollback triggers and a simple post-flight checklist for post-mortem enrichment

ENG: implement JSON schema and validation library in repo redwood/launch-readiness (Marcus)

SRE: author production health probes and capacity reserve signals; add to telemetry pipeline (Ava Chen)
DES: design dashboard tile and failure states for Console UI; provide assets and copy (Riley)
PM: write rollout gating rules and approve canary thresholds (Priya)
ENG: wire the preflight job into Launch Conductor as a pre-cutover hook (Marcus)
ENG: implement Slack and Console notifications with direct links to playbook and on-call (Sana)
QA: produce automated smoke test harness and sample prompt set for runtime regression tests (Jamal)
DOCS: create Confluence runbook, examples, and emergency rollback checklist (Lina)
Post-launch: schedule 1-week follow-up to collect metrics and adjust thresholds (Priya)
Retro: include postmortem template fields for scorecard signal drift and test flakiness (Marcus)
risks: False positives from flaky smoke tests could block rollouts — require noise analysis and retry/backoff
Score thresholds may not generalize across model sizes and regions; need weight-by-workload config
Integrating into Launch Conductor may reveal timing delays for long-running preflights
Dashboard UX could be misunderstood by non-technical stakeholders without clear copy
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable for runtime/console/api changes in staging -> small canary (10%) for 2 weeks; observe signal drift. Phase 2 (pilot customers): opt-in Dedicated customers and one internal product team. Phase 3: default-on for all non-hotfix rollouts with ability to opt-out for emergency patches. Gate configuration and thresholds stored in Launch Conductor config and editable only by PM+SRE leads.
comms_plan: Pre-launch: announce in #product-launch, #sre, and weekly All-ENG memo; invite SRE/Platform to dry-run. Day-of: automated message to #launch-alerts with score and link. Escalation: if score fails for >2 consecutive runs, page on-call SRE and route to on-call PM. Post-launch: summary email with metrics and any action items.
qa_runbook: Smoke tests: canonical prompt set for generation QPS=10 for 60s; validate 95th percentile latency, token rate, and qualitative hallucination sample check. API tests: run integration tests against staging endpoints; validate 5xx < 0.1% and 4xx within expected. Console tests: load Console tile and validate display and link resolution. Failures recorded to incident tracker with reproducible steps.
estimated_cost_impact: Minor recurring CI job cost (~$200/month) and additional telemetry retention (~$500/month) until thresholds stabilise
